correspondence.component_scope: Chosen Chillihua–Huacuyo opening
correspondence.finding: The chosen northeastern opening lies on the continuous blue upper corridor labelled Qda. Chillihua. The original sheet follows its northward bend beside Pampa Chillihua and the Quillo Apacheta setting, then the westward Huacuyo-labelled turn. The chosen approach is distinguished from the more southerly Japu/Otora and Cuellar/Coline branches. The map shows the actual connected upper course, rather than only a basin label.
correspondence.named_reach_scope: Named upper quebrada corridor, without assigning an exact naming transition

correspondence.component_scope: Sajeno corridor to the Otora receiving valley
correspondence.finding: The selected westward and southwestward continuation follows the original Sajeno-labelled channel past the Anoccollo, Huayllane and Sajena/Sajena Alta setting. It reaches the Otora-labelled valley at the Porobaya-side junction. The southern Porobaya branch is separately drawn; its name is not transferred to the selected northern opening. The blue course remains continuous across both selected part boundaries.
correspondence.named_reach_scope: Qda./Río Sajeno and Río Otora reaches

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Otora and Chujulay confluence
correspondence.finding: The map carries the selected Otora course through Inogoya Chico and Peche, then into the clearly mapped junction with the separate eastern Río Chujulay near Higuerane. The receiving southward reach is labelled Río Huaracane. The selected bends and the junction into Huaracane are observed in the original cartography.

correspondence.component_scope: Huaracane, Torata and Tumilaca joins beside Moquegua
correspondence.finding: The selected course continues south through the Huaracane valley and its Siete Vueltas/El Chorro setting, receives Río Torata from the Yacango–Molesaja side, and enters the Moquegua valley near Loma Quemada and La Chimba. The separately mapped Tumilaca approach from Yunguyo joins the same downstream receiving corridor near the Moquegua urban-valley setting. The report identifies the Ilo-Moquegua river below the Huaracane–Torata confluence. Tumilaca and its Asana headwater are tributary context, not the chosen opening.
correspondence.named_reach_scope: Río Huaracane into the representative Ilo-Moquegua river

correspondence.component_scope: Moquegua valley through the cultivated southern corridor
correspondence.finding: The original map follows the selected receiving river past San Francisco, Sorzano, San Antonio, Los Anillos, Cruz Verde and the Corpanto/Santo Domingo corridor, then the Sacata–San Julián–Taquila valley. The depicted river remains distinct from roads, piezometric contours and adjacent seasonal side quebradas. Every selected interval here falls on the connected blue valley channel.

correspondence.component_scope: Taquila and Molle into the middle gorge
correspondence.finding: The original blue course runs past Taquila, Villalobos and Molle and continues through the gorge around Pacayanto and Angelina toward La Capilla. Both the broad valley-to-gorge transition and the longer southwestern continuation are depicted without an unlinked interval. Groundwater symbols and alluvial shading are not used as substitutes for a surface-channel through-link. The source establishes a mapped river corridor, not present perennial discharge.
correspondence.named_reach_scope: Río Moquegua, within the downstream Osmore naming context

correspondence.component_scope: La Capilla and Osmore lower-gorge continuation
correspondence.finding: The mapped receiving course continues southwest from La Capilla past the Osmore Chico/Osmore Grande setting, receives the distinct Guaneros-side drainage and continues into the lower valley toward Santo Domingo and Hernández. The source report explains the downstream Osmore and Ilo naming sequence. The nearby Guaneros canyon remains a tributary, rather than an alternate selected outlet.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Ilo valley approach
correspondence.finding: The original sheet follows the selected lower course through the valley east of El Algarrobal, including the approach past the Chiviquingua/Loreto Viejo setting. The blue river connects the gorge exit and cultivated lower valley continuously. Adjacent Honda and Chibora quebradas and the separate coastal drainage north of the mouth are distinguished from the selected receiving river.

correspondence.component_scope: El Algarrobal to the actual Pacific terminal
correspondence.finding: The final selected part follows the original Ilo-labelled channel through El Algarrobal, Chiribaya, El Magueo, La Glorieta and Uruhuasi to the coast at Boca del Río/Peña Blanca, immediately north of the main Ilo port setting. The original map visibly connects the channel to the Pacific coastline, and the report explicitly gives the Pacific as the terminal receiving body. This establishes the actual selected river-mouth corridor at ordinary scale, without requiring the offshore rendering extension or present shoreline to match exactly.
correspondence.named_reach_scope: Río Ilo mouth in the Boca del Río–Peña Blanca setting

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen interior opening and first westward/southwest through-link
correspondence.finding: The chosen opening and its initial westward bend lie in Ilha Charapucu interior. The two maps do not establish a continuous connection from this opening into the mapped southwest-going tributary. Nearby island/park membership and broadly connected regional drainage cannot fill this link.

correspondence.component_scope: Mapped southwest-going tributary and western turn into Furo Charapucu
correspondence.finding: From the portion where the interior tributary is depicted, both maps support its southwest-going continuation and selected western turn into the southern Charapucu waterway. No hydronym is assigned to the unnamed interior tributary.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern Furo Charapucu bends and eastward return
correspondence.finding: The selected long southern passage and return east are depicted as connected Furo Charapucu reaches. This is a named furo/channel passage around Ilha Charapucu, not evidence for a uniform river name on the initial interior tributary.

correspondence.component_scope: Northward transition into Cajari and selected fragment join
correspondence.finding: The eastern end of the southern channel turns north into the depicted Cajari corridor. The transition between stages3 and2 is on this continuous mapped channel. Exact name-change vertices are not assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Cajari–Afuá northern interconnection
correspondence.finding: Original cartography depicts the chosen continuous northward channel, its bends and side joins toward Afuá. FAPESPA explicitly relates Charapucu to Cajari and Afuá. The route is described as an estuarine channel connection without inferring present flow direction, navigation conditions or a single name across every reach.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual selected northern terminal
correspondence.finding: The selection ends on the named Afuá corridor north of the city in the channel between Ilha Pirauara and Ilha Cajuúna. The source maps depict this channel continuing toward Baía do Vieira Grande beyond the selected endpoint; that further bay reach is not added to the selection.

correspondence.component_scope: Lake, reservoir and managed passages
correspondence.finding: No selected through-lake, reservoir or engineered-control passage is depicted on the inspected corridor. The meaningful mapped passages are interconnected island channels/furos. The headward gap remains separately stated; absence of detailed operational evidence is not used as a reason for pending status.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen opening, northward hook and southeastward inland-ice sequence
correspondence.finding: The chosen western opening lies in mapped Inland Ice at the western side of Dronning Louise Land. The complete initial northward hook and subsequent southeastward series lie within the broad ice terrain beside small exposed-rock outliers, approaching the larger exposed-rock margin. The actual first twenty parts and their intermediate joins are covered in continuous original cartography. Ice contours and the surrounding nunatak geography do not establish a river or its name.

correspondence.component_scope: East-southeastward ice and exposed-rock transition
correspondence.finding: The next selected sequence enters the generalized western exposed-rock margin of Dronning Louise Land, among mapped ice-margin indentations and colored bedrock areas. The source covers the whole succession and its southern bend. This is geographic ice/land correspondence; the selection is not thereby a surveyed channel across the mapped rock and ice boundary.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle eastward and reverse-bend passages
correspondence.finding: The selected line turns northeastward and then southeastward through the middle exposed-rock and intervening pale ice-margin passages of Dronning Louise Land. All twelve parts, their turns and joins are geographically exposed in the original. The adjacent blue ice contours and mapped land boundaries are not river lines or proof of surface or subglacial throughflow.

correspondence.component_scope: East-northeastward exposed-land sequence
correspondence.finding: The complete east-northeastward continuation occupies the generalized eastern exposed-rock tract before the final southeastern turn. The original shows the surrounding bedrock units, ice-margin incisions and the relation to the broader Storstrømmen setting. It supplies uninterrupted ordinary-scale geographic coverage, but no hydronym or continuous mapped natural-watercourse identity for this selected succession.

correspondence.component_scope: Southeastern turn toward the eastern margin
correspondence.finding: The selected southeastern turn and each short following part remain within the eastern exposed-rock/ice-margin setting. The source accounts for the entire approach to the lower eastward segment. Nearby closed pale patches and water/ice boundaries are not taken to prove a selected lake-throughflow or a named river reach.

correspondence.component_scope: Final eastward passage and actual selected ending
correspondence.finding: The final five parts continue from the eastern exposed-rock margin toward the broad pale ice/coastal-water setting on the southwestern Dove Bugt side, south of the main Storstrømmen label. The preceding land margin, final eastward continuation and actual supplied ending are all present in the original at ordinary regional scale. The model sea-terminal label does not establish an ordinary river mouth. Exact present-day ice-front, bank and terminal land/ice/water assignment are not claimed.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen southwestern delta opening
correspondence.finding: The chosen opening is already in a thin interior delta channel east of Macareo, north of the wider southern river-and-lake setting. The source depicts the selected north/northeastward feeder continuously through this southwestern interval. It is not substituted with the broader western Macareo or the southern Río Grande/Sacupana routes. A historical aeronautical overlay crosses near the opening, but the underlying channel and onward connection remain distinguishable. The model beginning is not declared the natural source of a river.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper branching and eastward dogleg
correspondence.finding: The source distinguishes several parallel and joining small channels. The selected feeder turns east/northeast through the characteristic short bends, then follows the middle dogleg toward the next receiving channel. Enlarged original linework shows the through-connection rather than merely a nearby name anchor. Unselected southwestern, southern and western arms are not added to the selection, and the stored-part boundaries are not treated as official channel-name boundaries.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle junction and northeastward wetland reach
correspondence.finding: After the eastward dogleg, the selected route turns north and northeast along the continuous narrow wetland channel. Its junction with the eastern northbound receiving reach and the successive middle through-links are visible. The separate farther-west channel continuing toward Macareo and the farther-east delta arms can be distinguished. No separate hydronym is established for this whole narrow interior interval.

correspondence.component_scope: Broad named mariusa receiving corridor
correspondence.finding: The thin middle channel enters the broader northeastward waterway directly labeled CAÑO MARIUSA. The chart shows the broad channel, a small internal island and nearby lateral arms. It separates this selected channel from Caño Macareo to the west and the Güiniquina and Araguabisi waterways farther east. The representative identity is grounded in this named receiving corridor and its mapped connection to the selected feeder.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower northward bend and terminal junction
correspondence.finding: The lower channel turns north along the eastern side of the Isla de Mariusa setting. Immediately before the coastal opening, a broad west/northwest-side arm along the island joins the selected approach. The source depicts that meaningful final deltaic junction and the final small bend to the coast. The selection ends here; it does not continue northwest around the island or turn into an eastern neighboring outlet.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual atlantic terminal
correspondence.finding: The actual selected tip reaches the charted coastal opening beside the southeastern end of Isla de Mariusa. The mouth setting is observable independently of the model sea classification. The chart supports the final river-to-coastal-water transition but no separately named barra, precise current shoreline vertex or formal mouth boundary is assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Wetland and small waterbody scope
correspondence.finding: The chart depicts a branching lowland delta-waterway setting and nearby small lakes. The selected through-route is mapped as connected channel linework rather than a required lake or reservoir crossing; the nearby southern small-lake field is not silently added as a selected passage. The authored state chapter independently describes the delta network and floodplain/coastal environments and lists Mariusa among the central-delta caños. These regional observations do not establish present tidal direction, uninterrupted modern surface flow or operating/navigation conditions.
